messages:
alex: noticing a spike of ECC/Xid alerts from dcgm-exporter on a few hosts in us-west-2. cc @mai @samira
mai: saw that too, mostly on gnode-12 and gnode-17, errors are short bursts not constant
samira: logs show repeated "Xid 31" and ECC single-bit increments, last seen 2h ago on gnode-12
alex: infra-bot posted alerts at 1749123100: dcgm_xid_errors_total > 0 (host: gnode-12) — noisy though, a lot are single-sample blips :confused:
mai: could be transient power/thermal spikes. But we had a ReplacePlan from Q4 for gnode-17 (flaky card) so probably correlated
luke: question — do we want current alerting to be >=1 error -> page? It seems like a noisy rule. We should tune to avoid paging on momentary single-bit ECC increments
samira: agree. Two options: (1) make Prometheus rule require persistence (for: 10m) or (2) aggregate by gpu and only page if n gpus on node exceed threshold. Both are easy.
alex: thinking: keep short alerts to slack (non-pager) but only escalate to pager if it persists > 15m OR if >1 gpu on same host fails within 5m. That matches our SLO for hardware failures.
mai: propose new rule skeleton:
```
- alert: PersistentGPUXidErrors
  expr: sum_over_time(dcgm_xid_errors_total[10m]) > 0
  for: 15m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "Persistent Xid errors on {{ $labels.instance }}"
```
and a non-pager noisy alert:
```
- alert: TransientGPUXid
  expr: increase(dcgm_xid_errors_total[5m]) > 0
  for: 0m
  labels:
    severity: info
```

luke: also add grouping by `gpu_index` and `instance` so we can count distinct GPUs: `count_values("gpu", dcgm_ecc_error_count)` etc.
infra-bot: detected gpu label mismatch on gnode-17, metadata shows `gpu_id: 2` but exporter reports `gpu_index: 3` — possible driver remap (handled)
mai: good catch. We'll need to confirm driver/kernel mismatch — could cause metric duplication leading to false positives.
samira: operational plan for gnode-12 (where errors are most frequent):
- cordon node
- drain pods that are GPU-bound (kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data gnode-12)
- reprovision node on next maintenance window if errors persist after hardware power cycle
- if hardware still flaking -> open RMA with vendor and schedule replacement
alex: let's be cautious on immediate drains — only drain if persistent alert hits pager (15m) or if node has >1 gpu with errors within 5m. Otherwise add to watchlist.
mai: I'll open a small runbook PR with the exact drain commands + labels to set (`gpu==suspect`) and update the Prometheus rules repo. Link: <https://git.internal/repo/infra/alert-rules/pull/XX>
samira: can we add an annotation to alerts with a quick command to add node to watchlist and set `node_annotation=investigate`? small helper script would be handy.
luke: i'll write the helper in the infra repo quickscript `bin/annotate-gpu-node` — will add to PR
alex: action items: mai -> PR for rule changes and runbook (ETA: EOD), luke -> helper script + test infra-bot annotation (ETA: tomorrow morning), samira -> confirm driver/kernel mapping on gnode-12 and try power-cycle (ETA: 2h), alex -> monitor and unmute noisy alert channel for 24h :thumbsup:
mai: noting cost/ops: if we start replacing nodes we should prefer spare capacity in us-west-2a to avoid cross-az traffic + eviction costs. will coordinate with capacity planning.
infra-bot: alert silence created by alex for TransientGPUXid for 24h (silence id: s-101)
alex: thanks — keeping this thread for updates. if anyone sees a steady rise in `sum_over_time(dcgm_ecc_error_count[15m])` across multiple hosts escalate immediately.
mai: will post PR link when ready.
